title: Read Now – Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: September 2026 Edition
content:
Nepal floods: how measuring snow in the Himalayas could help avoid future disasters

The August 2026 glacial flood that killed more than 1,000 people on the Nepal–Tibet border has renewed urgent calls to close a critical knowledge gap: scientists still do not know precisely how much water the Himalayas hold, or how fast that is changing. Home to nearly 90,000 glaciers sustaining ten major river systems, the region underpins the food, energy and water security of six nations. New measurement techniques, including airborne glacier surveys and satellite radar measurements, are emerging, but deployment remains too slow and too sparse. Researchers argue this must be treated with the urgency of a public emergency, with scientific innovation matched by coordinated monitoring networks, cross-border data sharing, and Indigenous knowledge.

Water investments, capital mobilisation, and national water compacts

title: CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan
content:
CDIF DCAT-Syntax Core and Discovery Profiles: Development Plan: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22942627 

This document is the first in an irregular series of updates on development plans for the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF). It briefly outlines the status and intended process for development of CDIF Core and Discovery profiles based on the W3C DCAT specification, as opposed to Schema.org. While Schema.org was initially chosen as the basis for core CDIF metadata, given its widespread adoption and support in various search engines and other widely used Web-based applications, the need for a similar foundation implemented using DCAT has become apparent, as its adoption is now becoming much broader.

The intention is that a point-for-point correspondence between the two sets of profiles — for DCAT on the one hand and for Schema.org on the other — can be established, and that free converters provided to enable users to produce and consume either flavour as needed. While a single agreed standard is always ideal, it is not in this case a reality, so this approach is seen as necessary.
